3-1-divisions-of-the-nervous-system-and-.label: Question 14
3-1-divisions-of-the-nervous-system-and-.exp: Only reverberating pathways send impulses back to earlier neurons in the pathway, which keeps the activity going.

3-1-divisions-of-the-nervous-system-and-.label: Question 10
3-1-divisions-of-the-nervous-system-and-.exp: The sympathetic branch speeds up the heart, and its neurons release noradrenaline at the SAN.

3-1-divisions-of-the-nervous-system-and-.label: Question 16
3-1-divisions-of-the-nervous-system-and-.exp: Structurally, the nervous system is central and peripheral (X). Functionally, the somatic system controls skeletal muscle (Y) and the autonomic system controls smooth muscle (Z).

3-1-divisions-of-the-nervous-system-and-.label: Question 18
3-1-divisions-of-the-nervous-system-and-.exp: The brain and spinal cord form the CNS; the somatic and sympathetic systems are part of the PNS.

3-1-divisions-of-the-nervous-system-and-.label: Question 18
3-1-divisions-of-the-nervous-system-and-.exp: In reverberating pathways, later neurons link back to earlier ones so impulses repeat.

3-1-divisions-of-the-nervous-system-and-.label: Question 18
3-1-divisions-of-the-nervous-system-and-.exp: Sympathetic neurons of the autonomic system increase heart rate and breathing rate.

3-1-divisions-of-the-nervous-system-and-.label: Question 19
3-1-divisions-of-the-nervous-system-and-.exp: The parasympathetic branch increases peristalsis and intestinal secretions.

3-1-divisions-of-the-nervous-system-and-.label: Question 18
3-1-divisions-of-the-nervous-system-and-.exp: One neuron branching to many neurons is a diverging pathway, which allows fine motor control of the fingers.

3-1-divisions-of-the-nervous-system-and-.label: Question 16
3-1-divisions-of-the-nervous-system-and-.exp: Pathway 3 has two neurons joining one (converging), pathway 1 has one neuron branching to two (diverging), and pathway 2 loops back (reverberating).

3-1-divisions-of-the-nervous-system-and-.label: Question 20
3-1-divisions-of-the-nervous-system-and-.exp: At 80 years, females have about 64 000 km of myelin, below 100 000 km, so conduction is slow and responses are slow.

3-2-the-cerebral-cortex-incl-perception-.label: Question 16
3-2-the-cerebral-cortex-incl-perception-.exp: People expect hearts to be red. This expectation (perceptual set) slowed recognition when the colours were swapped.

3-2-the-cerebral-cortex-incl-perception-.label: Question 16
3-2-the-cerebral-cortex-incl-perception-.exp: Smaller trees look further away (relative size), higher trees look further away (relative height), and trees in front hide others (superimposition).

3-2-the-cerebral-cortex-incl-perception-.label: Question 18
3-2-the-cerebral-cortex-incl-perception-.exp: Repeating the whole procedure with more groups shows whether the results can be reproduced, which tests reliability.

3-2-the-cerebral-cortex-incl-perception-.label: Question 19
3-2-the-cerebral-cortex-incl-perception-.exp: The corpus callosum is the band of nerve fibres connecting the two cerebral hemispheres.

3-2-the-cerebral-cortex-incl-perception-.label: Question 19
3-2-the-cerebral-cortex-incl-perception-.exp: 'Spoon' is seen by the right eye and goes to the left hemisphere, which controls speech. 'Fork' goes to the right hemisphere, which cannot pass it across.

3-2-the-cerebral-cortex-incl-perception-.label: Question 21
3-2-the-cerebral-cortex-incl-perception-.exp: Each visual field is processed by the opposite hemisphere: the left pattern goes to the right hemisphere and the right pattern to the left.

3-2-the-cerebral-cortex-incl-perception-.label: Question 19
3-2-the-cerebral-cortex-incl-perception-.exp: The corpus callosum passes information between the left and right cerebral hemispheres.

3-2-the-cerebral-cortex-incl-perception-.label: Question 20
3-2-the-cerebral-cortex-incl-perception-.exp: Balance is coordinated by the cerebellum, not by the association areas of the cerebral cortex.

3-2-the-cerebral-cortex-incl-perception-.label: Question 17
3-2-the-cerebral-cortex-incl-perception-.exp: Language processing and memory recall are cerebral cortex functions. Breathing and heart rate are controlled by the medulla.

3-2-the-cerebral-cortex-incl-perception-.label: Question 18
3-2-the-cerebral-cortex-incl-perception-.exp: The corpus callosum links the hemispheres, and the left hemisphere processes the right visual field.

3-3-memory.label: Question 15
3-3-memory.exp: Spatial memories, such as a route around a room, are stored in the limbic system.

3-3-memory.label: Question 15
3-3-memory.exp: Spatial memories are stored in the limbic system.

3-3-memory.label: Question 17
3-3-memory.exp: The injury interrupted short-term memory before the events could be transferred to long-term memory.

3-3-memory.label: Question 20
3-3-memory.exp: Middle items are recalled least because new items displace them from short-term memory before they reach long-term memory.

3-3-memory.label: Question 19
3-3-memory.exp: S returns information from long-term memory (retrieval), Q moves it into long-term memory (encoding), and R loses it from short-term memory (displacement).

3-3-memory.label: Question 20
3-3-memory.exp: Elaboration and organisation help encode information into long-term memory. Chunking increases short-term memory span.

3-3-memory.label: Question 20
3-3-memory.exp: Chunking improves short-term memory capacity. Rehearsal, elaboration and organisation encode into long-term memory.

3-3-memory.label: Question 19
3-3-memory.exp: Ages 51–80 in 2019: 5123 + 5600 = 10 723, which is more than any other year.

3-3-memory.label: Question 21
3-3-memory.exp: 8 out of 12 items is 66·7%, which rounds to 67%, not 66%. The other three statements match the graph.

3-3-memory.label: Question 22
3-3-memory.exp: Middle items are lost from short-term memory because later items displace them before they are transferred.

3-4-the-cells-of-the-nervous-system-and-.label: Question 15
3-4-the-cells-of-the-nervous-system-and-.exp: Alcohol is removed at 16 mg/100 cm³ per hour. Falling from 240 to 80 is a drop of 160, which takes 10 hours.

3-4-the-cells-of-the-nervous-system-and-.label: Question 20
3-4-the-cells-of-the-nervous-system-and-.exp: Acetylcholine is released (4), diffuses across the cleft (2), triggers an impulse (1), and is then broken down by an enzyme (3).

3-4-the-cells-of-the-nervous-system-and-.label: Question 21
3-4-the-cells-of-the-nervous-system-and-.exp: Glial cells produce the myelin sheath and support neurons.

3-4-the-cells-of-the-nervous-system-and-.label: Question 21
3-4-the-cells-of-the-nervous-system-and-.exp: Antagonists block receptors, so the brain makes receptors more sensitive. This contributes to addiction.

3-4-the-cells-of-the-nervous-system-and-.label: Question 22
3-4-the-cells-of-the-nervous-system-and-.exp: Dopamine agonists bind to dopamine receptors and mimic dopamine, making up for the low levels.

3-4-the-cells-of-the-nervous-system-and-.label: Question 21
3-4-the-cells-of-the-nervous-system-and-.exp: Blocking the dopamine reuptake protein keeps dopamine in the synapse longer, overstimulating the reward pathway.

3-4-the-cells-of-the-nervous-system-and-.label: Question 22
3-4-the-cells-of-the-nervous-system-and-.exp: After the second injection, dopamine falls by about 65% every 20 minutes (245 to 180). Continuing to 120 minutes gives about 115%.

3-4-the-cells-of-the-nervous-system-and-.label: Question 20
3-4-the-cells-of-the-nervous-system-and-.exp: The fall increases by 2 mg/L each hour (2, 4, 6, 8), so the next fall is 10 mg/L: 16 − 10 = 6.

3-4-the-cells-of-the-nervous-system-and-.label: Question 19
3-4-the-cells-of-the-nervous-system-and-.exp: Endorphins stimulate neurons that reduce the intensity of pain.

3-4-the-cells-of-the-nervous-system-and-.label: Question 23
3-4-the-cells-of-the-nervous-system-and-.exp: Antagonists block receptors, so receptors become more sensitive. Repeated exposure this way leads to addiction.

3-5-non-specific-body-defences.label: Question 19
3-5-non-specific-body-defences.exp: Histamine causes vasodilation and makes capillaries more permeable, so more blood and fluid reach the damaged area.

3-5-non-specific-body-defences.label: Question 23
3-5-non-specific-body-defences.exp: Cytokines released at the infection site attract phagocytes, causing them to accumulate there.

3-5-non-specific-body-defences.label: Question 21
3-5-non-specific-body-defences.exp: Mast cells release histamine (2), causing vasodilation and leaky capillaries (4), so blood flow increases (1) and phagocytes accumulate (3).

3-5-non-specific-body-defences.label: Question 23
3-5-non-specific-body-defences.exp: Mast cells and phagocytes are part of non-specific defences. Lymphocytes are specific.

3-5-non-specific-body-defences.label: Question 21
3-5-non-specific-body-defences.exp: Mast cells release histamine, which starts the inflammatory response.

3-5-non-specific-body-defences.label: Question 22
3-5-non-specific-body-defences.exp: D starts in the normal range, peaks at 15 000 at day 2, falls to 3000 at day 4, then rises gradually back into the normal range by day 10.

3-5-non-specific-body-defences.label: Question 24
3-5-non-specific-body-defences.exp: Mast cells release histamine (R), blood flow increases (P), phagocytes accumulate (Q), and they release cytokines (S) to attract more.

3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.label: Question 17
3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.exp: The TB bacterium survives inside phagocytes, so it is hidden from the specific immune response.

3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.label: Question 19
3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.exp: In autoimmune disease, T lymphocytes respond to the body's own (self) antigens.

3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.label: Question 20
3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.exp: W rises and stays high (leukaemia), X rises above 11 then falls back (leucocytosis), and Z drops below 4 (leucopenia).

3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.label: Question 19
3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.exp: Z has extra mast cells (allergy), X has fewer lymphocytes (HIV destroys them), and Y has extra phagocytes (infected wound).

3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.label: Question 19
3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.exp: Influenza changes its surface antigens (antigenic variation), so memory cells no longer recognise it.

3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.label: Question 23
3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.exp: In MS, T lymphocytes attack the myelin sheath, so impulses travel more slowly.

3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.label: Question 22
3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.exp: Autoimmune diseases happen when T lymphocytes respond to the body's own self-antigens.

3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.label: Question 24
3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.exp: T lymphocyte numbers stay level between years 4 and 5, so they do not decrease continuously.

3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.label: Question 22
3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.exp: A hypersensitive response to a harmless foreign substance is an allergy, and B lymphocytes produce the antibodies involved.

3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.label: Question 24
3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.exp: B lymphocytes produce and release antibodies.

3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.label: Question 23
3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.exp: At 3 years, T lymphocytes are about 100 per mm³ (left axis) and HIV is about 50 thousand per mm³ (right axis).

3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.label: Question 24
3-6-specific-cellular-defences-against-p.exp: 10 cm³ contains 70 000 white blood cells. Split 7 : 3, that is 49 000 phagocytes and 21 000 lymphocytes.

communication-and-social-behaviour-2015-.label: Question 16
communication-and-social-behaviour-2015-.exp: Performance changed when others were present (fewer errors when competing). That is social facilitation.

communication-and-social-behaviour-2015-.label: Question 18
communication-and-social-behaviour-2015-.exp: At 8 years the brain has done about 95% of its growth and the skeleton about 55%. 95 : 55 simplifies to 19 : 11.

communication-and-social-behaviour-2015-.label: Question 17
communication-and-social-behaviour-2015-.exp: 12 months lies between the 25% mark and the 50% mark on the bar, so a bit under half of 24 infants (about 10) would walk.

communication-and-social-behaviour-2015-.label: Question 18
communication-and-social-behaviour-2015-.exp: Working in the presence of others improved performance on a simple task: social facilitation.

communication-and-social-behaviour-2015-.label: Question 18
communication-and-social-behaviour-2015-.exp: Group 2 copied a demonstration, so they learned by imitation.

communication-and-social-behaviour-2015-.label: Question 17
communication-and-social-behaviour-2015-.exp: Fear of one insect has spread to all similar insects: generalisation.
